notes:
I couldn't do this research. On my first attempt, the search tool returned an error saying I had no more tool calls left for this turn. A second try gave the same error, so I didn't get to search or read a single page.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written any notes. Anything I wrote now would come from memory, with URLs I hadn't checked, and that is exactly what you asked me not to do.

**When the tools are working again**, this is the plan:

1. **Verse-by-verse sources:** the Enduring Word page for 1 Samuel 21; the BibleHub/StudyLight pages for each verse (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary, Matthew Henry); Precept Austin's 1 Samuel 21 page; and the NET Bible notes.
2. **Topics likely to show differences between traditions:**
   - **vv. 1–2 and 8:** whether David's lie to Ahimelech was wrong, and how it led to the killing of the priests in chapter 22. I'd look at Reformed, Baptist, Wesleyan and other sources on the sites you listed.
   - **vv. 4–6:** the consecrated bread, and how Jesus uses this story in Matthew 12, Mark 2 and Luke 6 to show that mercy comes before ritual. I'd check Lutheran (1517.org, lcms.org), Reformed and Catholic readings.
   - **vv. 10–15:** David pretending to be mad at Gath, and the link to the headings of Psalms 34 and 56. I'd look at Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* and Desiring God.
3. **Other views:**
   - **Modern scholarship:** NET Bible and Bible Odyssey notes on the Ahimelech/Abiathar question in Mark 2:26 and on the "holy equipment" wording in v. 5.
   - **Catholic and Orthodox:** New Advent (Church Fathers on David and the bread) and Catholic Answers on Mark 2:26.

Please send the request again, or just say "go", and I'll run the searches and write the notes with a source link for every point.
